text_fidelity_a:
CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes I started playing Settlers of Catan when it first came out, many years ago. It has a special place as a gateway game. It brought people who wouldn't normally play anything exotic out of the world of Chutes and Ladders, and into the realm of strategy board games. It's easier to learn than Monopoly, but without the very lengthy period of regret between knowing who will win and actually reaching the foregone conclusion. I largely stopped playing the game about 20 years ago because thanks to Catan, the world of board games exploded into a great variety of games that I consider to be much better. Seeing this fancy set made me want to give it a try again, see what might have changed, and teach the kids.

Unboxing:
The components are visible in the packaging, which is unusual. The outer box is a throwaway, but there is a good sturdy box inside. Everything is packed well enough to avoid shifting and scuffing in transit. There are a few too many components for my taste. It takes quite a while to get everything taken out and put away. I'm fine with that if a game really needs that level of complexity, but I think this one is pushing it. The new three dimensional components make it even more of a chore. I like that the water border clips together securely. In the original, the water spaces tended to slide around, and since the game is about building roads and houses on the cracks, it was destabilizing for everything. Now the board stays together securely, even on carpet.

The new three dimensional tiles are a fun idea, but poorly implemented. Each one needs a convex, translucent, slippery disc on top, but few allowances were made for this in design. They just teeter there and slip around, or sit way off center. I can't support making the number circles translucent. I can't see any positive purpose for it, and it reduces the ability to play with variants that start with some of them face down. After assembling the sea sections, I see that the game board is smaller than I expected. I really like the addition of harbor shapes on the seas to show where the ports should go. The ports themselves are a bit hard to see compared to the old cardboard ones.

The colors chosen for each player are questionable. The parts themselves have a dark wash over them to make the details stand out, but it makes them all dingy. Beige, orange, red, and blue. I guess the blue player can find their pieces, but in dim lighting, the rest look too similar. There's an odd mix of unique things, like the shape of each player's houses, and having things repeat that could have been unique, like all of the forest hexes being identical.

If the instruction book is hard to open, it's because it isn't a book, it's a foldout that folds counterintuitively. There is a quick reference startup guide and another small book with more in-depth details.

It's nice that it comes with card holders, and while it's a chore to get everything back in the box right, at least there's a secure place for everything. The gameplay is as I remember. Simple and engaging enough for most people to be willing to play, and strategic enough to be satisfying. There are games that are both simpler and more strategic out there. Quite a lot of them. In a four player game, anyone who ends up hemmed in by players who chose after them can end up stuck without anywhere to expand. This leads to occasional games like Monopoly, where someone isn't going to be having much fun for an hour. Luck can play a bit too heavily. This was one of the early games that added the excellent mechanic of randomizing the playing field, but the dice too often just end up rolling the same number over and over, which tends to give some players a lot to do and others nothing for several critical turns.

It's strange, but I think I may actually stick with my old plain set. This one feels more fancy and less functional.
text_fidelity_b: CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!

-- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. [[ASIN:B00JBP32A0 JST JST-XH 3S Balance Wire Extention 20cm adapter 11.1v LiPo Battery Cable Li-Po]] This also allows you to put the cells into a fireproof bag during charging. [[ASIN:B005Q3VSZC Bluecell Black Medium Size Lipo Battery Guard Sleeve/Bag for Charge & Storage]]

One other accessory that really helps is a compact voltage indicator [[ASIN:B003Y6E6IE Integy C23212 Lipo Voltage Checker/Warning Buzzer]] that you plug into the balance port on the battery. Not strictly needed for recharging, but is very useful to monitor voltage after charging.

You'll need to consult YouTube for useful instructions on how to manipulate the four buttons and why, unless you want to read the manual. And who reads manuals anymore when a good ten minute video is clearer and simpler?

6' Giant Teepee Play House of Pine Wood with Carry Case by Trademark Innovations (White) purchased for my grandsons to use when visiting..... it is large.... large enough for an an adult to get into. The material is a cotton canvas... not terribly thick, but not too thin in my opinion. It was relatively easy to put together... I like that this is a bottom floor attached. It is quite popular to stay grandma's and camp out.... I added some "nap pads" which are perfect for the 5 and 2 year old. It does come with a handy bag that has a handle if you'd like to store it when not in use. The poles are wood... a pine I believe... very sturdy. I would recommend this teepee... I always update if there are any issues that may be helpful.
3/25/2016 UPDATE: ...so I just finished deconstructing the teepee and felt an undate with tips might be helpful... first... you will never get the canvas teepee back into the canvas bag provided... it's like folding/rolling a really thick fitted sheet and trying to get into a tube sock.... BUT the wooden poles fit nicely into the canvas bag along with the plastic connector pieces... it would have been nice if the connectors gripped the poles better and stayed connected during the deconstruct phase... however... I just removed all the holed top pieces and then turned the teepee upside down and shook it sort of like a pillow case... the lower pieces eventually come out... I just rolled the teepee up, put all the poles and connector pieces in the bag and set in a large drawer I have. I would have lowered my rating one star for the deconstruct hassle, but honestly, my grandsons love it so much I just can't. The quality is such that this is going to last for many years if we take care of it. It's just a matter of learning how to use it in an efficient manner. Also... I have hard wood floors, so I went to a local carpet store and purchased some carpet padding. I cut into a circle and place it under the teepee when I have it set up... I worry less about bonked heads that way - grandsons 5 years and 2 years. Ok! Hope this is indeed helpful info!

Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray) For my daughter's sake, I would give this camera 5 stars. It is the longest lasting favorite toy any of my kids have ever received, EVER. I bought it for my then 7 year old daughter for Christmas 2 years ago, and it is still her very favorite toy at age 9. She plays with it almost daily, takes it with her on trips and to important events, and shows everyone the pictures she takes. I think not much more praise can be had for a toy than for it to be beloved after two full years of daily play! But I wills say, her expectations for it are different than mine. She doesn't care about printing the pictures out. She likes taking them and looking at them on the viewfinder, projecting them on the wall, and using the added features to make funny frames around the people and funny sounds. That's all she wants from it, and it delivers that perfectly.

BUT, as a parent, I would have hoped the screen would be better quality. When you look at it, it's sort of blurry and got lines through it. Frankly, sometimes it's hard to tell what I'm looking at. This doesn't bother my now 9 year old daughter AT ALL. But it is disappointing to me because I know the technology exists to make that better.

The quality of pictures is also not great when uploaded onto my computer (which I've only done a couple of times). It's VERY pixelated. Again, this isn't a feature my daughter cares about, so take that into account, but for me I wish that the option were there to print out a decent quality print because sometimes she takes really awesome shots that I wish I could save.

This camera is also super tough. Despite being dropped and thrown around and fought over by siblings for the last 2 years, it still works perfectly. The batteries last her generally a few months, depending on play. But they're just AA's, so no biggie to change them out.

Really, I am most impressed that this toy continues to make her so happy. I think Playskool could go a long way to making the picture/screen quality better, even for kids, but that's just a mom talking!
text_fidelity_b: Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray)

LEGO Architecture Skylines: Tokyo 21051 Building Kit, Collectible Architecture Building Set for Adults (547 Pieces) This LEGO ARCHITECTURE SKYLINES: TOKYO 21051 BUILDING KIT (New 2020 ; 547 Pieces) took me longer to assemble than it should have, because the building instructions are printed in white on a black background. The model’s base uses black LEGO pieces, so you need very good light to decipher the white-on-black drawings at the beginning. I’ve assembled numerous LEGO sets, but had to restart this one after seriously misinterpreting the instructions for the base.

Other than that, the Tokyo architecture model is interesting and fun. There is quite a bit of studs-not-on top assembly, and there are some very innovative connective techniques. Happily, the elements are printed with the graphics (no stickers to apply).

Thanks to the innovative, amazing architecture that exists in real-life Tokyo, the finished model makes a terrific display piece. For some reason, I really like the back wall of the model, which represents Mount Fuji. The finished model is small enough to fit easily into a bookcase or wall-mounted display case.

The instruction booklet includes photographs of the actual Tokyo buildings that are represented. In addition, short text paragraphs (in English, French, and Spanish) explain the functions and backgrounds of the buildings.

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. I had almost forgotten about this little loom -- I first learned how to make these potholders in the 1950s even before I started school (I was probably 5 yrs old). My brother and I spent many summers working on these and selling them around the neighborhood to augment our $0.25/week allowance. My mother taught us how to make them and kept us supplied with the loops while we came up with our own designs.

One thing I remember very clearly -- she avoided nylon loops, preferring instead cotton loops. Why? Because the nylon loops could melt at the temperatures commonly encountered when using cast iron pans and metal baking dishes in hot ovens. I retained that memory, so when I saw this kit available with cotton loops, I knew I needed to try it one more time.

The major difference I see is in the length of the "prongs" in the loom -- I recall them being a little longer. Also, the metal weaving hook was a bit longer. But other than that, the design and construction are close to what I used as a child.

The package from Amazon arrived earlier today, and I quickly put together the potholder in the photo. It took probably an hour -- perhaps a bit longer, but not much. There are enough loops for a couple of pot holders and enough colors to mix and match. Follow the directions, especially the part about finishing -- pulling one of the loops on each finished edge back over a loom peg to keep the rest of the loops on the adjacent and opposite sides from popping off the loom. Take your time with this part -- it's easy to want to hurry to finish it, but it can be a bit "fiddly."

Very happy with this -- I've already ordered additional loops in specific colors to coordinate with my kitchen colors so I can make several of these to use as potholders as well as hot pads/trivets.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll I have been around Barbie dolls my entire life. My mom collected them and my sister got into it. My daughter has had a few here and there, but none of them was the quality that this doll is. I did not expect it to be fantastic quality, but it even fell short of my lower expectations.

WHAT IS THE DOLL LIKE?
The doll comes in a clear plastic package which is not overly attractive, in fact it looks stark and not like the usual Barbie stuff. The doll itself is packaged with two pieces of plastic sticking out from inside her head. It is then attached to the board in the back so you have to cut those pieces to get it off of the backing. That means you have to be careful of the hair. Once you managed to do this, you have to stick the plastic ends back into the skull of the doll to keep the sharp ends from pricking your child or you.

The outfit is kind of cute and the colors are attractive. The doll itself is a rigid plastic doll- not the bendable twist and turn type that they have had in the past. The head piece has a knob type attachment which makes it able to move in almost any direction. The problem is in this case, the head is so easy to move it is borderline bobble head.

HOW DOES THE HAIR COLOR WORK?
The hair color looked like it would be a lot of fun! It has a plastic piece that is similar to a flat iron in shape. Inside the *flat iron* piece are a group of colored waxy blocks. The idea is that you comb the doll's hair and separate it into strands. You press the flat iron type piece over the hair, squeeze it shut as you draw the hair through and it leaves the color on the hair.

The hair is waxy in feel, probably to make the color work better than traditional Barbie hair. In this case, however, it does not seem to do much for the process. The hair colors are not too great. They come off as crumbly and waxy and very spotty on the hair. If you run your fingers over it, you will get some on your fingers. This will stain so if your child plays with this near anything white or light colored, it could stain it.

The color blocks are almost like you mix waxy crayons with silicone to make it a bit softer. The result is uneven kind of unimpressive color on the hair. It is not overly bright and does not look like the pictures promised.

THE BOTTOM LINE
My daughter was not impressed by this doll. The body is very rigid, making for a boring play toy. The hair is very uneven and has a waxy feel to it. The colors come out crumbly and uneven, and color blocks probably will only last for a day or two of constant play and then run out. The colors will stain some things so if you plan to let your child run free with this, you may regret it if you have anything white you don't want stained. The head is so easily moved that it is unpleasant to play with and use. The outfit is cute and colorful and the shoes are not too bad either.

My daughter kept saying that she expected more substantial color that was like a watercolor marker or something instead of a crumbly waxy substance that barely sticks to the hair in a few random spots. She kept taking out her other Barbie dolls and saying how much more she liked those. I give this two stars because it has a nice outfit, and if you want a disposable toy for your child, it will serve the purpose. If you want a sturdy toy they will play with over and over, I am thinking this might not be it for you.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

text_fidelity_a:
Adora Playtime Collection Pink 13 Soft Baby Doll with Bottle This is a sweet, tiny baby girl doll about half the size of your average newborn. I expected the feet, hands, and head to be ever so slightly softer than they are, but it's not so hard that you'd be upset if you fell over on it or had your big brother bash you with it, hopefully accidentally.

The baby powder fragrance is a little overwhelming to start, but I'm hoping that will settle down in time. I'm not really used to a lot of artificial fragrances so it's definitely a lot stronger than any other scented item in our home. The fragrance is overall pleasant, just a little too much. It really sticks to your hands, too. I played with the doll for just a few minutes with my son, and after washing my hands twice with Dr. Bronner's peppermint soap, I can still smell the artificial baby powder fragrance.

The baby bottle included doesn't look very realistic in the sense that the entire thing is made of a pale pink plastic, so there's nothing that looks "milky" in there. There's also no differentiation between nipple, lid, and bottle. That said, it does fit into the baby's mouth and stay there nicely. I like that the baby's body is made of the silky material kind of like a ribbon, and the outfit she is wearing is easy to take off and put on for little hands. I wish there was not printing on the front of the shirt, as I'm not sure a baby doll needs to say "pretty girl" on the front. My son really enjoys taking off the headband and putting it back on.

The eyes open and close and if not perfectly upright, the baby has a generally heavy lidded disposition. The one unnerving thing is that when the eyes are opened/the baby is angled too quickly, the eyes make a clicking sound when the lids open fully. I wish they'd done a little more design testing to eliminate that minor flaw, because my toddler son was immediately entranced and wondered what the noise was and it caused some not very gentle experimentation with flipping the baby around to see what was going on with the sound.

Even with what I see as a few minor design flaws, overall this is a very sweet, nicely sized baby doll for a young one aged 1 to 3, and would be a good doll to put in a miniature baby carrier or generally to carry around and play with. I wish I had thought to get a doll like this prior to my son's baby sister arriving so that he could practice playing gently with doll and nurturing the doll.
text_fidelity_b: Adora Playtime Collection Pink 13 Soft Baby Doll with Bottle

Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy The Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is an educational toy in the shape of a clock, made from wood, with small wooden sorting blocks that fit into designated spaces. This toy helps to teach kids how to tell time and match shapes and it makes a great toy option for youngsters in the preschool age group.

Educational toys are the preferred toy from a parental point of view, but it is sometimes a challenge to find an educational toy that my girls will enjoy for an extended period of time. With the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock, it appears I have achieved victory in this area. Even weeks after their initial encounter with this toy, my girls still enjoying sorting the blocks and reading the numbers on the clock dial. Each of the blocks is colored differently and shaped differently and my girls enjoying figuring out which block fits into which slot.

One of the many advantages with the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is its ability to educate in multiple ways. Not only does it teach kids spatial skills and how to tell time, it also teaches kids how to match numbers, count the minutes and hours, and arrange the hands of the clock to a certain time. With the blocks, younger children will have two ways to match: By shape or by number. If they cannot match the number, they can match the shape that fits, thus eliminating frustration and eventually learning the number in the process. Yet another advantage of this toy is that it encourages more imaginative play. There are no bells or whistles and no batteries. The hands of the clock are moved only by pushing with the fingers. These facts make the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock a little on the old- fashioned side, in a sense, but in a positive way.

Educational toys are the best but it is often a challenge to find an educational toy that children will enjoy. This toy has passed the test with flying colors, offering satisfaction to both child and parent. It is true that the small blocks can get lost in due time, but other than this, the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is an excellent toy overall. It teaches children several skills and offers great durability, is made from wood, and requires no batteries. My little ones love it and continue to enjoy it day after day. It's an easy winner that belongs in every child's toy box.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy

text_fidelity_a: Pass the Stache Board Game Watching a group of 13 year olds play Moustache Smash is like watching a Black Friday sale with everyone fighting for the same discounted towels. I couldn't help but laugh hysterically as each girl held the mustache up to her face then frantically tried to be the first to smash the card that either matched the color or the shape of their mustache. (Mind you they had to remember which mustache they chose and what it looked like because they have to keep it up on their face at all times when the game is in play - until it's time to snatch a card). The game comes with 6 mustaches on very solid plastic sticks. There is a suction cup at the end of the mustache that allows the playing card to be snatched up quite easily. It's best to play on a solid surface to make sure the card stays put. There are 32 mustache cards of various colors and shapes. Each player takes a turn being the dealer. The dealer flips the card over for all to see - but can't cheat by flipping the card facing them first. IF a player accidentally snatches up the wrong mustache, they have to return it plus two more mustaches (if they have them) from their stash. It goes into a pot for the next player who correctly snatches up a mustache to claim. When all 32 cards are dealt, the game is over. The player left standing with the most 'stashes wins. The cards are in perfect squares - keeping the field even for all players. The mustaches feel rubbery so are less likely to cause harm if accidentally smacked into another players hand. The one thing I suggest is you have the camera at the ready! I have some great video and excellent pictures that I was able to share with the players' parents. Unfortunately, without the parents' permissions, I cannot display any of the videos or photos. They weren't comfortable with their children being seen. The recommended age is 7 and up, but I can easily see a 5 year old handling this well. I would also be willing to play with a group of adults. For $15.99 with free prime shipping, it is a great birthday or Christmas gift without breaking the budget. Plus, there are no tiny pieces to lose or step on. (BONUS!)  Keep in mind, though, that there are only 6 mustaches... so a max of 6 players can play at one time.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories There are really only two things one need know about any Schleich product in my experience.
1) They’re a bit pricey.
2) You get what you pay for.

The brand oozes quality and that holds true with the barn as well. It’s compact, well-made of quality material, and is smoothly fluid in all its moving parts. It comes hinged together and easily opens up to reveal a nice size play area. The wood is real and solid, the paint job nicely finished. The windows, corral doors, and back door open and close smoothly and easily, and the large doors in the back slide open and shut, also smoothly and easily. It comes with a large cow, a lamb, a donkey, and a rooster, each of them quite solid and hefty in the hand. And again, nicely finished and detailed. A few accessories complete the package--a bale of hay, a crate of apples, a pitchfork and a broom.

Really, as mentioned at the start, there isn’t much to say about Schleich beyond the fact that quality quality quality is the mantra. Based on our experience with other Schleich products, I imagine this barn and its animals will give years of imaginative play regardless of how often or how hard that play is. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is a fun toy that encourages creativity and keeps kids occupied. This stamp kit comes complete with nine different stamps, a small ink pad with pink and purple ink, and five colored pencils for your child's creative enjoyment.

Melissa and Doug toys are known for education, creativity, and durability and most every product the company makes can be counted on to posses at least two of these qualities. The same is true with this toy. The Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set isn't big on educational quality, but it does encourage creativity and the set and storage container are made from wood, for better durability. The wooden container offers easy storage so that pieces do not get lost and the product's individual pieces are designed to last.

Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is simple yet fun and requires little supervision or explaining. My little princesses like this toy and still find it fun, but I have noticed that it lacks the staying power of some of their favorite toys. Unless I suggest it, they are not likely to use it. They do like it, but I think they have become a little bored with it. They prefer toys with movement and sound, and this offers neither.

This stamp set is certainly durable, but one thing that isn't made to last is the ink pad. I like that the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set comes complete with its own ink and my girls strongly appreciate that the ink is colored purple and pink. However, don't expect the ink to last very long. The small blotches of ink will not offer many stamping adventures, so be prepared to purchase additional ink stamps within a few months.

Although not the perfect toy, the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is nonetheless a good toy for little princesses everywhere. It has many positive qualities, encourages creativity, and is priced right. Like I said, it lacks staying power, but it has enough positive qualities to recommend.

Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+ If you, like me, are looking for games to play with a high energy, lack of focus little boy, then this is the game for you. For my four year old, games with a lot of rules and that require skills he's still learning with clear winners and losers are not the best choice games for us. He doesn't have the patience, skill, or temperament. I needed games to slowly introduce him into those skills and Pop Up Pirate is that game! The only rule, everyone takes turns to place a sword into a slot. The person who makes the pirate pop-up out of the barrel wins. We don't play winner/loser, but you can if you choose to do so.

The game comes with 20 swords, four colors with five each, a barrel, and said pirate. It's for 2 to 4 players, my son and I just pick up a sword no matter the color, but if you have more kids or players, then you can choose colors. You stick the pirate in the barrel where there is a trap/spring mechanism that is only triggered when someone sticks a sword in the right slot. Each player takes a color and everyone takes turns sticking a sword into a slot. When the right sword pokes the pirate, he pops high up into the air. The pirate is fairly light weight so if he were to really go flying he would not break anything or hurt anyone. The pirate jumps at most 2 feet into the air, probably less. The only caveat is to make kids aren't sticking their face near the barrel with the pirate in the hole for obvious reasons. This game comes in fairly big box as the barrel is about as wide as a clothes iron, but not nearly as tall.

If you need a game for toddlers/preschoolers that is guaranteed to teach taking turns and highly giggle inducing, then Pop up Pirate is your game!
text_fidelity_b: Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+

Lost Cities - The Board Game You can move your five explorers (you don't need to use them all) on any of five paths. You can move one square forward on each color if you play a card of that color that is higher than the last card you played. So if you play a two, you can play a three or a four etc, to move forward. You can't play a lower card, but you can discard it, and your opponents can pick it up. Along the way you get bonus points and artifacts to raise your score. Three rounds makes a game.

This game is supposed to take 30 minutes to an hour, but I have yet to find even a three player version go that fast. There is too much strategy and planning involved. You need to think about what cards you need now, what you need later, what your opponents might use if you discard a card, and how many "for later" cards you can retain. You need to decide when to bite the bullet and take a big number jump (limiting your later moves) and when to hold off.

It definitely plays better with more than two players. It's fast to learn, and a lot of fun.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game

It also comes with sleeves - one set for Mewtwo, and the other for Melmetal, which is strange considering that he's not in the box.

I just started playing the game with my nine year old daughter, and the one deck will certainly help add to our collection of decks, but you need to know what you're buying here. The Battle Academy set includes three decks, not two, and is similarly priced to this set, and will give you multiple "how to play" books that will help teach you the ropes. I'd start there.

Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

Aqua Oversized 8 Foot, Scorch The Dragon, 4 Mode, 16-Color LED Light-Up, Ride On, Inflatable Pool Float Lounge With a large in-ground pool in my backyard, we spend a good deal of time outdoors. The pool is great for cooling off during our hot Gulf Coast summer season and we have a fair number of pool toys to keep us entertained. The Aqua Flash Scorch the Dragon LED Light Up Pool Float is our latest addition to our growing and expanding number of pool accessories.

This pool float is large in size and can hold two young kids with ease. You just inflate, add the lights, and you’re ready to go. There are no batteries included, so you will likely need to run to the store to purchase some, since each of the puck lights requires three batteries. Pick up a large pack of alkaline batteries and you should be all set.

With its large size, this float makes an imposing presence in the pool, but the coolest aspect of this float is the added lights. It comes with a remote control so you can switch the patterns around, from strobe to fade to flash to smooth. My kids like the lights more than anything. They already have plenty of other floats, but none of them have lights like this. During the evening hours, the flashing lights really help to spruce up a party. I did notice that the float does lose air after a few days and we have to re- inflate, but this is common with most floats and isn't an important issue.

Aqua flash Scorch the Dragon LED turned out to be hugely popular with my family and it has been a great addition to our pool. There is no shortage of pool floats on the market, but the difference with this float is the lights. They really add to the float’s appeal and make it an excellent choice as your next pool accessory.

Spontuneous - The Song Game - Sing It or Shout It - Talent NOT Required - Family Party Board Game… Spontuneous is a fresh, clever & fun new family board game. You start by coming up with a list of words. Each word needs to be found in a song. Then once a word (trigger word) is given, the first person to come up with the lyrics that uses that words (in a phrase/line of at least 5 words) gets to roll the dice & advance. My 14 year old daughter LOVED the game. Even after our game was finished, she begged us to keep throwing out trigger words for her. She can't wait to play it with her friends. My 17 year old son is not a fan of most family games and although he did play with us, he couldn't wait to finish. He claimed that he didn't know enough songs to play. My husband & I both enjoyed it, though we did find that the 15 second allotment was hard at times. The directions weren't too complicated which was a big plus! There are challenge cards to get if you land on a certain spot. There was one penalty card which you could use if you caught someone on their cell phone! The game is designed for 4-10 players and is relatively short with games lasting about 30 minutes. It was interesting how we would all come up with different songs for each trigger word!

*I received the game for the purpose of trying out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.
text_fidelity_b: Spontuneous - The Song Game - Sing It or Shout It - Talent NOT Required - Family Party Board Game…

Battat – Wild Ridge Train – Classic Wooden Toy Train Set with Mountain Top Lid, Double-Sided Tracks, Toddlers 3-Years-Old & Up (47Pc) Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington This wild ridge train set is a decent set, compatible with most other wooden tracks such as Thomas and friends. The price is pretty good for the amount of tracks you get.. the main reason I only give it 3 stars is because most of the track pieces are not reversible (only have tracks on one side). We have several other sets like this and almost all of the pieces are reversible in the other sets. Having non-reversible pieces really limits the amount of configurations you can do.

Also the connection between some of the pieces is rather loose which tends to cause the train to derail, especially if those loose pieces are placed near a bend. Some of the other sets we have had loose pieces also but this one seems to have more loose pieces than most.

BIC Magic Marker, Flexible Brush Tip (4.5 mm), Assorted Colors, Kids Coloring, 220-Count Bulk Pack For Kids This is an awesome set of really nice markers. Be aware that the dividers holding all of the different markers in separate containers is not actually attached to the bottom in any way, so your order will almost certainly arrive with the markers disorganized, as mine did. However, a bit of tape and a jellybean bounty to the children soon put that right.

The line is a good clean line and the tips seem resistant to fraying when mushed a little too hard by small hands. The color saturation is very rich and worked well on the notebooks that we keep for coloring.

The highlight of this set is that the markers are advertised as not drying out when exposed to the air when children leave the lids off. If you have small children, you'll know that "put the cap on it" is a constant and tiresome refrain, so for families or teachers, this is a huge and thoughtful benefit. While I didn't test keeping the lids off for 90 days, a couple of overnights assured me that for more normal, temporary times of the lids being off, the markers are not prone to drying out.

Overall this is a fantastic set for teachers or homeschoolers who go through more than the usual amount of art supplies. It would also be great for a party where coloring a themed item is part of the event.
